Sara / Chris — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Below are Redwood's proposed positions (we tried to be prescriptive so your auditors have clear language):

1) Retention — customer content vs telemetry
- Customer content: archived and retained per customer-specific retention schedule. Unless Customer specifies otherwise in writing, Redwood will retain customer-provided content for the duration of the customer's active service plus 30 days to allow for export and orderly deletion.
- Telemetry / operational logs: Redwood collects telemetry for service quality and security. Default retention is 30 days; Redwood can extend telemetry retention to 90 days for specific telemetry categories upon written agreement (see attached Retention_Schedule_ZenithAI.xlsx).

2) Backup / DR carve-out
- Redwood will create backups for the purposes of disaster recovery and service continuity. Backups may contain customer content but will be encrypted at rest. Redwood proposes the following ceiling for backup retention: backups will be retained for a maximum of 90 days from creation unless otherwise agreed in writing. Backups older than 90 days will be destroyed or overwritten in normal operating processes, except where retention is required by law.

3) Subprocessors
- We confirm EdgeCache Solutions is listed as a subprocessor on our public registry (link below). EdgeCache provides CDN edge caching; it does not have access to decrypted customer content outside of encrypted transit and operates under contract clauses consistent with our DPA.

4) International transfers
- Redwood uses Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) where required for EU transfers and maintains a record of transfer mechanisms. We can provide executed SCCs or a controller-to-processor addendum on request.

If Zenith can accept the 90-day backup ceiling and the retention schedule above, we can incorporate the language into a clean DPA and move to DocuSign. If Zenith requires a 60-day backup ceiling, please let us know and Neha can scope a commercial concession.
